claims.text: The target material is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix.
Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation will improve the wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
A nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation has been deployed in Ni50(AlNbTiV)50.
The proposed architecture will protect the FeNiCrCoCu coating through a multi-type adaptive friction interface governed by nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates.
The cooperative nanoscale structure will release gradient frictional stress during wear.
The proposed architecture will activate a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer during wear.
The modified coating will have better wear resistance than the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating under identical test conditions.
The modification may reduce wear rate by an order of magnitude relative to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The wear-resistance prediction applies from room temperature to 800 °C.
The wear-resistance prediction applies from low to high friction velocities.
The wear-resistance prediction applies from shallow to deep wear depths.
The exact magnitude of the wear-resistance improvement is uncertain.
The optimal parameters of the nanohierarchical architecture remain uncertain.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing architectured and unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coatings under otherwise identical sliding conditions.
Failure of the architectured coating to achieve a significantly lower wear rate than the unchanged coating would falsify the hypothesis.
